lines.text: A rules file is plain Markdown the agent reads at the start of every session.
Claude Code calls it CLAUDE.md.|Codex and many other agents call it AGENTS.md.
lines.say: Claude Code calls it Claude dot M D. Codex and many other agents call it agents dot M D.

lines.text: Put in it what you'd tell a new teammate:|build commands, conventions, where things live, and what never to do.
Rules load from broad to specific.
Your organization's file, then yours, then the project's,|then any folder below it, once the agent works there.
They're combined, not replaced, and the closest one is read last.
All of it is sent with every request,|so every line costs context, every time.
It says: use pnpm, not npm, and run the tests before committing.
An @ import pulls in another file,|like the AGENTS.md your other tools already read.
lines.say: An at sign import pulls in another file, like the agents dot M D your other tools already read.

lines.text: And a rule in .claude/rules can carry a paths field,|so it loads only when the agent touches matching files.
lines.say: And a rule in dot claude slash rules can carry a paths field, so it loads only when the agent touches matching files.

lines.text: Keep it under two hundred lines.|Longer files cost more context, and get followed less.
Imports organize a file, but they don't shrink it: imported files load too.
If two rules contradict each other, the agent may pick one arbitrarily,|so prune them.
Codex reads AGENTS.md,|and stops adding files at thirty-two kilobytes by default.
lines.say: Codex reads agents dot M D, and stops adding files at thirty-two kilobytes by default.
